newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Gilt vol softer ahead of heavy data week.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Gilt vol softer ahead of heavy data week.

text.p: Implied volatility of gilt options was slightly lower on Monday ahead of a week packed with UK economic data, options brokers said.

Volatility on July gilt options exercisable into the September gilt future was at 6.92 percent, according to figures from a British broker. August was at 6.99 percent, September at 7.14 percent and December at 7.04 percent.
Gilt volatility in the front month has drifted down around half a point from the middle of last week, before Friday's quarter point rise in official UK interest rates.
September gilt futures were trading at 113-29 at 0940 GMT, down 5/32.
"We saw the gilt market trading up on a rate rise," said Peter Bygrave, senior floor broker at Lloyds Bank. "The market is pleased to get the rate move out of the way."
Options traders said they will look to a wealth of UK economic indicators due this week.

Following May producer price data and stronger than expected April industrial production and manufacturing data released earlier on Monday, gilts will focus on May unemployment data and April average earnings data on Wednesday.
Unemployment will fall by 40,000 and average earnings will come in at 4.50 percent, a Reuters survey showed.
May retail price data will be released on Thursday, and is forecast to gain 0.3 percent year on year.
Options volume was thin early on Monday, said one broker from a European firm, though there was two-way business.
In gilt options, activity centred on July 114-00 calls, July 117-00 calls and September 117-00 calls.
